newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: SM Prime 9-mth net seen at 1.35 bln pesos.
newsitem.headline: SM Prime 9-mth net seen at 1.35 bln pesos.

text.p: Mall developer SM Prime Holdings Inc is forecast to post a 30 percent rise in net profits to 1.354 billion pesos in the first nine months compared with the year-ago 1.039 billion pesos on the back of higher retail sales by its tenants, according to a Reuter poll of four brokerage houses on Tuesday.
For the full-year 1996, consensus shows net income is projected to rise by 27 percent to 1.925 billion pesos from 1.510 billion pesos.
In the first half of 1996, its net grew by 32 percent to 858.8 million pesos from 651.5 million pesos.
Consumers' higher purchasing power from more jobs and lower inflation are driving up SM Prime's earnings, analysts said.
"People are spending more," said Noel Reyes, research head of Anscor-Hagedorn Securities.
Reyes said he recently upgraded his forecast for SM Prime for the full year to 2.1 billion pesos from 1.917 billion pesos.
The country's per capita income rose 14 percent to $1,060 in 1995 from $931 in 1994.
About 85 percent of SM Prime's mall revenues comes from a percentage of its tenants' sales, while 15 percent consists of fixed rent.

"SM Prime is working under a favorble demographic environment," said Fred Rivera, an analyst of ING Barings Securities. Apart from higher disposable incomes, the increasing rate of urbanization in the country is boosting SM Prime's revenues, he said.
"From 37.5 percent (of the population) in 1980, the number of urban dwellers have increased to 50 percent," Rivera said.
Analysts say their forecast for SM Prime now takes into account the full-year operation of Southmall, which added leasable spaces of 119,190 square metres (sqm). It started operations in April 1995.
SM Prime operates five malls, four of which are located in strategic places in Manila and one in central Philippines.
It is the biggest shopping mall operator in the country with over 500,000 sqm of leasable space and a high occupancy rate of 98 percent, analysts said.
SM Prime ranked number eight in terms of market capitalisation at the Philippine Stock Exchange at the end of September.
